description: Generate /home/workspace/zo_mesh/zo_lifecycle.py — a tiny stdlib-only Python module that every long-running daemon imports at startup to emit structured lifecycle events. This is the foundation for two larger workstreams: (1) the tower-side harvester pattern (consume lifecycle JSONL via Syncthing, produce fleet-level reports), and (2) the RLSD-style training corpus (lifecycle events are sparse environment-direction signals — 'this daemon ran cleanly to completion' = success, 'crashed mid-tick' = failure — that we will later pair with token-level magnitude signals from frontier teachers). MODULE CONTRACT: exposes exactly five public functions: emit_starting(daemon_name, version='unknown', extra=None), emit_ready(daemon_name, extra=None), emit_tick(daemon_name, work_done=None, extra=None), emit_warning(daemon_name, reason, extra=None), emit_stopping(daemon_name, reason='shutdown', extra=None). Each writes a single JSON line to /home/workspace/logs/lifecycle/<daemon_name>-<pid>.jsonl with schema: {ts: ISO8601 UTC, daemon: str, pid: int, event: 'starting'|'ready'|'tick'|'warning'|'stopping', version: str, work_done: optional dict, reason: optional str, extra: optional dict}. CRITICAL: failure of the lifecycle emit MUST NEVER crash the calling daemon — wrap every file IO in try/except, log to a fallback /home/workspace/logs/lifecycle/_emitter_errors.log on failure, return cleanly. The lifecycle dir is created on first emit if missing. PID is captured at module import time (os.getpid()) and used as the file suffix so multiple instances don't clobber each other. NO HEARTBEAT POSTING TO service_health — that's a separate concern owned by each daemon's own heartbeat thread; lifecycle is a parallel signal stream, not a replacement. NO IMPORT OF requests or any network library — this module must work even when write_service is down. NO IMPORT FROM zo_mesh — sibling modules will import zo_lifecycle, not the other way around. Standard library only: json, os, sys, time, datetime, pathlib, traceback. Module ends with a __main__ block that runs a self-test: emit_starting + emit_ready + emit_tick + emit_stopping for daemon_name='zo_lifecycle_selftest', then reads back the file and prints success or failure. Self-test exits 0 on success, 1 on failure. INCLUDE: module docstring referencing the larger purpose (harvester foundation + RLSD direction-signal corpus), inline comments where the failure-isolation matters, and a 'WHY' comment block at the top explaining the design choice of file-per-pid JSONL over a single shared log (concurrent-write safety, harvester-friendly tail reading, easy archival). DO NOT INCLUDE: any reference to 'cron', any decorators that depend on third-party libraries, any class hierarchy — keep it five module-level functions plus _safe_emit helper. Total target: 120-180 lines including docstrings. Tests for this module are out of scope for this directive — a separate test_zo_lifecycle.py directive will follow.
